paragraphs: BusPatrol runs school bus stop-arm enforcement programs alongside school districts, municipalities, and law enforcement agencies. The company says communities can enforce the law around stopped buses at no upfront cost.

Cameras on the bus detect illegal passings and capture video evidence of them. Agencies review the results through dashboards, monthly reports, and compliance tools. The program also runs public awareness and public service campaigns meant to change how drivers behave.

BusPatrol states that it partners with school districts in 26 states. It says communities using the program see measurable reductions in dangerous driving around stopped school buses. The company traces its origin to a child killed while getting off his school bus in Ontario, Canada. Its staff, by its own description, includes technologists, retired police officers, and teachers.

quote.text: Communities across the country choose BusPatrol to modernize their school bus fleet.
